The Anthropic case raises a question governments would rather not answer: who has the authority to decide when a machine may exercise violence without human supervision?

u.El 8 de marzo de 2026, drones iraníes at: On 8 March 2026, Iranian drones struck three Amazon Web Services data centres in the Gulf. A twenty-thousand-dollar drone can shut down a billion-dollar facility: destroying the cooling system is enough. The servers then destroy themselves within hours. That asymmetry — cheap to attack, ruinously expensive to defend — is also the logic underlying the war's most improbable conflict: the legal battle between the Pentagon and Anthropic, the artificial intelligence company that refused to surrender control of its systems without conditions. The data centres burned because AI infrastructure is already military infrastructure. Anthropic went to court because it refused to let that equivalence be complete.
u.Anthropic llegó al enfrentamiento con el: Anthropic came to its confrontation with the Pentagon with two non-negotiable conditions: that its technology not be used for mass surveillance of American citizens, and that it not be used for autonomous weapons — systems capable of selecting and attacking targets without meaningful human intervention. These were not whims. They were the company's public policy, published, defended in congressional testimony, embedded in its public-benefit structure.
u.El Pentágono quería acceso para \"todos: The Pentagon wanted access for "all lawful purposes" and argued that it could not allow a private contractor to insert itself into the chain of command. Its chief technology officer described the problem in operational terms: if during a live mission an automatic limit triggered a refusal, soldiers would be left without intelligence support in the field. Dario Amodei met Secretary Hegseth on 24 February. They reached no agreement. On 27 February, the Pentagon designated Anthropic a national supply-chain risk — the same category reserved for Huawei, and the first time in history that designation had been applied to an American company. [National Catholic Register, 30 Mar. 2026; CFR, 5 Mar. 2026] Trump on social media: "I fired them like dogs." OpenAI accepted the same terms Anthropic had rejected, hours later.
u.El contrato con el Pentágono representab: The Pentagon contract represented less than one per cent of Anthropic's revenue. The company that had bet most heavily on integrating itself into the national security ecosystem ended up designated a risk to that very system.
u.Lo que ningún analista había modelado fu: What no analyst had modelled was what happened next. In the days after the announcement, Claude overtook ChatGPT in the iPhone App Store for the first time — on Saturday 28 February, climbing from 131st place in January to number 1, according to Sensor Tower data. [TechCrunch / Sensor Tower, 1 Mar. 2026; Fortune, 2 Mar. 2026] The company recorded the largest single-day number of new users in its history: paying subscribers more than doubled year to date and daily active users grew 167% in March compared with February. [Apptopia, April 2026] Bloomberg reported on 3 March annualised revenues on track for almost 20 billion dollars — passing 19 billion, more than double the pace of late 2025 — with growth driven mainly by Claude Code. [Bloomberg, 3 Mar. 2026] The public read the conflict with the Pentagon as a certificate of integrity.
u.Anthropic demandó al gobierno federal el: Anthropic sued the federal government on 9 March in two jurisdictions. Its lawyers warned Judge Rita F. Lin that more than a hundred corporate clients had contacted the company with concerns; one partner at the FDA migrated to a competitor, wiping out a hundred million in expected business. Estimated damage in 2026: potentially billions. Researchers from OpenAI and Google DeepMind — direct competitors — filed an amicus curiae brief in their personal capacities supporting it. So did Microsoft and retired generals. Their argument was strategic: a system that was never interrogated about its own limits is, in the long run, more dangerous than one that was. [National Catholic Register, 30 Mar. 2026; Washington Monthly, 2 Apr. 2026]
u.Nada de lo anterior convierte a Anthropi: None of the above makes Anthropic a disinterested actor. It is worth saying precisely, because imprecision here is costly: that a company has principles does not mean those principles are independent of its business model. Amodei's bet — building a recognisably ethical AI company as a competitive advantage — is simultaneously a moral stance and a differentiation strategy. Both things are true at once, and the fact that the market has validated them does not resolve the tension between them.
u.El problema estructural es este: las pol: The structural problem is this: corporate policies, however solid, are not regulatory frameworks. They can be reversed under sustained pressure, a change of leadership, or simply a sufficiently large offer. The same week Anthropic was designated a supply-chain risk, Claude was operating within Palantir's Maven system for intelligence assessments on Iran. Company policy and battlefield reality ran in parallel, over real cities, in real time. That is not necessarily hypocrisy. It is the limit of what a company can guarantee once its systems are already embedded in infrastructure it does not entirely control.
u.Lo que hace al caso Anthropic incómodo p: What makes the Anthropic case uncomfortable for its own defenders is that its virtue depends on its willingness to maintain that virtue under mounting pressure. A regulatory framework depends on nobody's willingness. That is precisely the difference between a company with principles and an institution with rules. The market rewarded the first. What the case exposes is the absence of the second.
u.La pregunta que el Estado no quiere resp: The question the state does not want to answer
u.El caso Anthropic no es sobre una empres: The Anthropic case is not about a company. It is about a governance vacuum that democratic governments have preferred not to fill. The underlying question — who has the authority to determine the threshold of violence a machine may exercise without human supervision — has been debated for more than a decade without producing any binding instrument. The UN Secretary-General set 2026 as the deadline for a treaty on lethal autonomous weapons systems. That treaty does not exist. In November 2025, 156 states voted in favour of a resolution urging negotiations. Five voted against. Consensus for a binding text has not appeared: China, France and the United Kingdom define autonomous systems differently. An entire arsenal fits in the gap between definitions.
u.En ese vacío, la regulación efectiva que: In that vacuum, effective regulation is delegated to the internal policies of private companies. That is not a solution. It is the problem. Corporate policies can be reversed by market pressure, a change of leadership, or governmental threat — exactly what happened to Anthropic. And while the litigation is resolved, the systems operate: the Wall Street Journal reported — confirmed by NBC News, CBS News and Bloomberg Opinion — that Claude was used by US Central Command for intelligence assessments, target identification and war-scenario simulation during the strikes on Iran, operating through its integration with Palantir's Maven system, even hours after the designation. [WSJ, 28 Feb. 2026; NBC News, Mar. 2026; CBS News, Mar. 2026; Bloomberg Opinion, 4 Mar. 2026] Company policy and battlefield reality ran in parallel, in real time, over real cities.
u.Lo que hace al caso políticamente incómo: What makes the case politically uncomfortable is that it exposes a contradiction states prefer to keep out of the courts: to use AI effectively in high-speed operations, systems need increasing degrees of autonomy. The more autonomous they are, the less compatible the technology of suppliers who refuse to cede that control becomes. The real choice is not between AI with limits and AI without limits. It is between designing legal frameworks that regulate autonomy before its proliferation makes them irrelevant, or continuing to improvise until the accident occurs that makes it impossible to ignore.
u.La apuesta de Amodei —que construir una: Amodei's bet — that building a recognisably ethical AI company would generate competitive advantage — is being validated by the market at the precise moment the government is trying to destroy it. But the longer story is not Anthropic's. It is that of the vacuum its case exposes: a world in which decisions about what may kill without asking depend on the resistance of a private company in San Francisco, and on what a federal judge decides. The vacuum is not an omission. It is a decision. And while the decision not to decide continues, the systems operate, the drones fly, and nobody in particular answers for what they do.
u.Una brecha que no cierra sola: A gap that does not close on its own
u.Hay un patrón que se repite cada vez que: There is a pattern that repeats every time a transformative technology outruns the institutions that ought to regulate it: society ends up depending, by default, on the ethical decisions of private actors. It happened with social media and disinformation. It is happening now with AI and autonomous violence. The problem is not only that normative frameworks move slowly — they always move slowly — but that in the interval, while legislators debate definitions and international bodies negotiate consensus that never quite closes, somebody has to decide. And that somebody, through the state's omission, turns out to be a company.
u.Lo que hace al caso Trump-Anthropic cual: What makes the Trump-Anthropic case qualitatively different from that familiar story is the direction of travel. This is not the state arriving late to regulate a technology that has already escaped. It is the state actively intervening to destroy the limits a private company imposed on itself — the only limits that exist at this moment. Designation as a supply-chain risk is not a policy for regulating AI. It is its opposite: the elimination of the only institutional friction available, exercised by an administration with no intention of replacing it with anything else. The result is not more state control over military AI. It is less control of any kind.
u.La paradoja es estructural: los gobierno: The paradox is structural: democratic governments cannot build normative frameworks for autonomous AI at the speed the market deploys the systems, but neither can they simply punish the companies that try to fill that vacuum with policies of their own. Either they develop the framework, or they accept that others will set it. What they cannot do — though they are doing it — is both at once: not regulate, and at the same time prevent those who do regulate from carrying on. The purpose of the line that heads this article is to remind us that this is not the first time the world has run into revolutionary technology. The nuclear age is a good example: different in impact but similar in risk. Remembering how it was addressed is essential to confronting this new scenario.
